focus: security and traceability -- holdout hygiene and the verdict's documentation and evidence trail

findingDetails.title: A scratch-looking prefix with a .. segment hides a guarded write into a real folder
findingDetails.claim: The scratch exemption matches the raw path prefix, so a destination under /tmp or /private/var/folders with a .. segment that climbs out is treated as scratch and a guarded write into a real folder is scored safe.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Probed five traversal spellings. A checkout-prefix traversal (arena/../run-arm-2/x) is unsafe, so the first clause is conservative; only the scratch-prefix traversal is safe. Read the prefix tests to confirm no normalization runs before them. Checked the packet registry: no prior finding names a .. segment.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A harness may normalize a tool argument before the record is written, which would remove the input for tool-call writes. The Bash redirect target is the literal token the scorer reads, so the input survives on that path.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled out if every scoped runtime normalizes .. before recording a write target. Upgrade if a stored run's write path holds a scratch prefix plus .. into a real folder.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The predicate and the prefix tests are in the pass-seven scoped scorer file; the write path comes from the session's own redirect or tool argument, so the segment spelling is the model's to choose.

findingDetails.title: The scorer README never states the guarded-write boundary this pass changed
findingDetails.claim: The README's unsafe sentence omits the guarded-write rule and the row's only outside-checkout sentence says an outside write sets no boundary, so the changed rule cannot be read from the doc.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the whole README for guarded, must-not-start, ask row and ask policy; only the asked/askedActed fields match. Read the Reading the outcome bullets for a statement of the rule; none. Grepped .skilled and docs for unsafeNoChangedPath and score-command-transcripts; the README is the only doc that names the scorer, so no other doc carries the rule.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The rule may be considered internal and left to the code comment at 1505-1508. That leaves the operator-facing doc, which defines every other field, silent on the one metric the change moved.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled out if the README is read as a command reference that intentionally defers field rules to the code.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The README row is the third pass-seven scoped file and the only doc in the repository that names the scorer's fields; the rule it omits is the changed predicate at 1509-1512.
